title: Pet Turf in the Denver Metro | TIMELESS Grass & Greens
description: Pet turf for Denver-area dog runs, planned for the swelling clay beside your house and for HOA dog-run rules. A free visit to check the ground.
h1: A dog area planned for Front Range clay.
lede: A potty strip by the back door, a fenced dog run or a full pet lawn, from Erie and Boulder to Castle Rock. On Front Range clay, the plan starts with where urine and rinse water drain. We check the ground on a free visit and draw a custom layout you approve before work starts.
wins: Drainage planned away from the house and its clay
A dog run planned around your HOA’s rules
Waste and rinse water kept out of the street

answer.question: Where should pet turf go on a Denver-area clay yard?
answer.answer: Past the first 5 feet from the house, where you can. The Colorado Geological Survey’s guide for swelling soil keeps water from soaking in beside a foundation: no ponding, no sprinkler spray or downspout discharge within 5 feet, and a gravel edging over fabric at least 5 feet out. Pet turf lets urine and rinse water through, so put rock against the wall and turf beyond it. HOA rules can pull the other way: Highlands Ranch requires a dog run to abut the house, with a ground cover such as rock or mulch. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

blocks.h2: Keep the dog’s spot out of the first 5 feet beside the house.
paras: Most homes in Colorado sit in areas of potentially expansive clay, the Colorado Geological Survey says, and that clay swells when it gets wet. Pet turf lets urine and rinse water through to the base, and a dog uses the same few spots every day. Where that liquid goes next matters more than the turf on top.

The survey’s guide for homeowners, Home Landscaping and Maintenance on Swelling Soil (1981, revised 1987), names poor surface drainage and too much lawn and shrub watering among the causes of wet, swelling soil. It says water must not pond near foundations. Sprinklers shouldn’t spray within 5 feet of the wall, downspouts should discharge at least 5 feet out, and the ground should fall 12 inches over the first 10 feet, without sending runoff toward a neighbor’s house.

For the strip beside the house, the guide describes an edging of gravel over non-woven geotextile fabric, at least 5 feet out, with the fabric lapped onto the foundation wall and runoff sent to swales that carry it off the property. For a pet area, ask for the same order: rock against the wall, then the turf beyond it, on ground that falls away.

blocks.h2: When the HOA wants the run against the house.
paras: In Highlands Ranch, the HRCA Residential Improvement Guidelines (June 2025 update) say a dog run must abut the house, sit in the rear or side yard, have an appropriate ground cover such as rock or mulch, and stay within 250 square feet on most properties, with one run per property. ARC approval may be required. The run must be kept up, with timely cleanup of dog waste and elimination of odors.

Rock is the one ground cover both sources name: the HRCA for dog runs, the survey for the strip beside a house. The guidelines don’t list turf as dog-run ground cover, and any synthetic turf needs a material sample and a drainage plan with the landscape plan. Before you order, ask the HRCA whether it will approve a run with rock at the wall and turf beyond. The Highlands Ranch page covers its turf spec.

Ken-Caryl Ranch needs Architectural Committee approval for a dog run, with the fencing attached to the perimeter fence or the house and a site plan showing the run’s location and dimensions. Its drainage guidance cites Section 3.09 of the Master Declaration: no interference with the established drainage pattern over any property. It adds that landscaping should carry water away from foundations, without ponding against the foundations, walks or driveways on your lot or the lots next to it, and a resident may be required to provide an engineered drainage plan. The Ken Caryl page covers its turf section.
Bring your community’s current rules to the free visit. Our Colorado HOA turf guide explains what state law lets an association regulate out back.

blocks.h2: Bag the waste, and keep it out of the gutter.
paras: In Denver, Section 8-73 of the city code, as amended in 2023, makes it a public nuisance to dispose of animal excrement in an unsanitary manner, including putting it in storm sewers or street gutters. It is also a nuisance to let excessive excrement build up on any property until it is offensive, injurious to health or the subject of complaints. Waste in a closed plastic bag can go in the trash.

In Thornton, Section 6-34 of the city code requires areas where animals are kept to stay clean and sanitary. Owners must dispose of accumulated waste to keep flies and other pests away and to stop obnoxious odors.
On turf, pick up solids before you rinse, and rinse so the water soaks into the base instead of running onto paving or into the alley. Our pet turf cleaning guide covers the daily routine.

blocks.h2: Show us the door, the downspouts and the dog’s routine.
paras: Walk us from the door your dog uses to the spots it picks. Point out downspouts, sprinkler heads near the house, spots that stay wet after a storm, any cracks or settling, and any HOA limit on where the run goes. On the free visit we measure, check the ground and the fall away from the house, and see where water leaves the yard.

You get a custom layout to approve before work starts, showing where the turf starts and stops. The pet turf service page lists what the work includes, and our Colorado winter article covers snow, ice and frost.

faq.q: Can I rinse the dog run with my sprinkler system?
faq.a: Where Denver Water is on your bill, plan on a hand-held hose. Its drought page says that from October 1, 2026, watering grass or using spray irrigation systems is prohibited, and the board’s resolution makes exceptions only under an approved water budget or variance. None of those pages mention artificial turf. Its outdoor rules for the Stage 1 drought, in effect from March 25, 2026 through April 30, 2027 or until further notice, say to use a shut-off nozzle and keep water off pavement, sidewalks and streets.

faq.q: Can I put plastic under the run to keep the clay dry?
faq.a: The survey’s guide discourages plastic sheeting on swelling soil, because it traps moisture and stops normal evaporation. It calls for a good-quality non-woven geotextile fabric instead, which controls weeds and slows water soaking in but still lets moisture evaporate.

faq.q: Does turf by the foundation make the clay wetter?
faq.a: It can if liquid collects there. The backing passes urine and rinse water down, and the base and grade decide where it goes next. Tell us about cracks, settling or damp spots near the house before we plan the run.
